attack_focus: characteristic generators and first/last active coordinates
parallel matroid elements / repeated coordinate classes
first/last bases and two-way chain condition

key_findings.detail: Classical minimal-trellis literature uses first/last nonzero coordinates or spans of generator ROWS to build/minimize the trellis for a fixed coordinate ordering. This is distinct from A3, which optimizes the ordering of coordinate/subspace OCCURRENCES and compresses repeated geometric COLUMN classes to first/last endpoint events.
key_findings.consequence: Do not confuse minimal-span/characteristic-generator first/last results with the A3 endpoint-class quotient. Treat them as close terminology/prior-art context requiring explicit distinction in the manuscript.
references: A. Vardy, Trellis Structure of Codes, Handbook of Coding Theory, 1998.
I. M. Duursma, Matrix Theory for Minimal Trellises, arXiv:1509.08376.
Kschischang-Sorokine / minimal-span generator matrix trellis constructions.

key_findings.detail: Cameron/Papadopoulos and Encheva-Cohen explicitly discuss generator matrices with repeated columns in the context of trellis complexity, first/last bases, efficient coordinate ordering and the two-way chain condition.
key_findings.consequence: Do not claim novelty for noticing repeated columns, relating them to trellis complexity, or using first/last bases/coordinate ordering to reduce trellis complexity.
references: P. J. Cameron, Codes, Matroids and Trellises, 2000.
S. Encheva and G. D. Cohen, Linear Codes and Their Coordinate Ordering, Designs Codes Cryptography 20 (2000).

key_findings.detail: The inspected trellis/minimal-span/TCC sources discuss optimal trellises for fixed order, chain conditions, sectionalization, repeated columns, first/last bases and coordinate permutations. No checked source stated an exact 2-state/3-state product quotient over distinct repeated column/geometric classes, the exact A3 transition count, or O(k*3^k) optimization parameterized by the number k of distinct geometric classes.

Classical sectionalization groups consecutive trellis sections to trade time-axis length against alphabet/branch complexity for a fixed code/order. A3 instead quotients the search over all occurrence orderings by class endpoint status. Sectionalization therefore does not directly subsume the A3 ordering DP.
references: A. Vardy, Trellis Structure of Codes, sectionalization section.

key_findings.detail: Kashyap formalizes trellis-width as pathwidth of the vector matroid of a generator matrix, so repeated generator columns are exactly parallel matroid elements. This confirms that the strongest prior-art attack language is parallel classes / repeated coordinates, not only coding-theory span-form terminology.
references: N. Kashyap, Matroid Pathwidth and Code Trellis Complexity, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 22 (2008).

high_risk_or_known: repeated columns occur in trellis/coding literature
class/type compression as a generic algorithmic idea
surviving_candidate: exact quotient of ALL occurrence layouts by per-geometric-class endpoint status
two states for singleton classes and three for repeated classes
O(k*3^k) exact bottleneck DP after 2^k subset-rank preprocessing, parameterized by number of distinct geometric subspaces

strongest_current_claim: For finite-field subspace-arrangement pathwidth, A3 supplies an exact quotient of the coordinate-occurrence ordering problem by geometric-class endpoint status and an exact O(k*3^k) DP after subset-rank preprocessing. Classical trellis span-form and coordinate-ordering literature is closely related but, in the checked sources, does not state or directly subsume this distinct-geometric-class product-state algorithm.
new_reviewer_killer_questions: Is there a coding-theory paper or thesis that explicitly optimizes trellis-width by first collapsing repeated/parallel generator columns into a 2/3-state per-column-class ordering DP?
Did Papadopoulos' thesis or the unpublished Bailey-Cameron-Papadopoulos first/last-base work contain an algorithm equivalent to the A3 class-endpoint quotient?
Is there a characteristic-generator or sectionalization formulation whose state graph is isomorphic to 2^s*3^r when coordinates are partitioned into repeated generator-column classes?
Is the distinct-column-class parameter k known under another name in trellis permutation literature?
